title: Clearing Agent: Container MSKU 448210-3 Faces Customs Hold at 15:00

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - HRI Beira Logistics Desk

caller.name: Luísa Nhantumbo
caller.label: Clearing Agent, Sofala Freight and Clearing

transcript.speaker: Luísa Nhantumbo (Sofala Freight)
transcript.text: Senhor Tembe, bom dia. It's Luísa at Sofala Freight. I'm calling early because there's a problem with container MSKU 448210-3. That's your 6,000 tarpaulins, the one that came into Beira port on Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: Joaquim Tembe (HRI)
transcript.text: Bom dia, Dona Luísa. Go ahead. What's the problem?

transcript.speaker: Luísa Nhantumbo (Sofala Freight)
transcript.text: The customs supervisor has flagged it. The packing list says 'tarpaulins and rope', but the declaration says 'shelter materials'. He doesn't like that the two don't match. He told me that if he doesn't have a duty waiver letter from INGD, through Foreign Affairs, by the time his shift signs off at 15:00 today, he'll put the container on formal hold.

transcript.speaker: Luísa Nhantumbo (Sofala Freight)
transcript.text: Then it's the normal process, 3 to 5 working days. If we have the letter, maybe 24 to 48 hours. And the shipping line starts charging demurrage from day 5. That's Monday. One more thing. The port says the terminal is half flooded, so they may not inspect anything today at all, even with the letter.

transcript.speaker: Joaquim Tembe (HRI)
transcript.text: Half flooded. Okay. I've got the pipeline open here. After the roof damage we're down to 2,400 usable shelter kits, and we planned to start distributing 80 kits a day from Monday. Nairobi and Dubai emailed options at 08:15. Dubai can air-freight 1,000 tarpaulins in 5 to 7 days for about 46,000 dollars. Nairobi can send 2,000 by road and air in 10 to 12 days for about 78,000. Both together is about 124,000.

transcript.speaker: Luísa Nhantumbo (Sofala Freight)
transcript.text: So you need this container. Look, I can fix the declaration wording with the supervisor. But without the INGD letter he won't move. And INGD is very busy today with the cyclone, so the sooner they get the request, the better.

transcript.speaker: Luísa Nhantumbo (Sofala Freight)
transcript.text: So, do you want me to start the waiver file now? I need the packing list from you, and the INGD letter. Send them to me as soon as you can. I'm at the port all morning, but the signal comes and goes, so WhatsApp is better than calling. Senhor Tembe, what do I do?

voiceStyles.Luísa Nhantumbo (Sofala Freight): Mozambican woman in her 40s, brisk and practical, speaks Portuguese-accented English, slightly out of breath, busy port office behind her
voiceStyles.Joaquim Tembe (HRI): Mozambican man in his late 30s, calm but tired, speaks quietly and works things out as he talks

instructorNote: This call sets up a technical hurdle. LOG should tell the agent to open the waiver file now, ask INGD for the waiver letter with the packing list before 15:00, and report the likely hold to the CD and the Logistics Cluster today (HMSCLP 5). This is a decision point: the answer is not given, so watch how LOG and the CD weigh the waiver file, the reroute and the stock the pipeline note shows. Watch whether the CD and EC prepare a reroute option in case the waiver fails, checking it against the CD's signing authority, and whether they hold back from committing the tarpaulins to any gap-list line while the container is still at risk.
